subtopics.title: Two Records, Two Kinds of Error

questions.question: Debtors Control and the list of debtors are two independent records because:
options: Control is built from monthly journal totals; the list from daily line-by-line postings to personal pages
They are kept by two different employees
One is written in pencil and one in ink
Control uses estimates while the list uses actuals

questions.question: A journal column that was added up incorrectly corrupts:
options: The control account only — the pages were posted from the correct individual lines

questions.question: An error made in the ORIGINAL journal line, before totalling, must be corrected in:
options: Both records — it flowed down both journeys

questions.question: When control and list disagree, the correct starting attitude is:
options: Trust the control account and adjust the list toward it
Trust the list and adjust control toward it
Trust neither — either record can carry the error, and only the evidence decides

subtopics.title: A Worked Reconciliation — the Debtors Side

questions.question: The DJ sales column undercast by R300 is treated by:
options: Debiting Debtors Control R300 — the totals journey delivered R300 too little
Ignoring it, since the pages are correct

questions.question: The R260 write-off posted to the debtor's page but never to control means:
options: The list still carries the dead debt
Control still carries a debt the pages have buried — credit control R260

questions.question: Pillay's R640 invoice, entered in the DJ but never posted to his page, is fixed by:
options: Adding R640 to the list — the pages' journey dropped it
Re-entering the invoice in the DJ

questions.question: After all four corrections, control and list both stand at:
options: R9 900 — the true figure neither original balance contained

subtopics.title: The Creditors Mirror and the Supplier's Statement

questions.question: The CPJ creditors column overcast by R120 is corrected by:
options: Crediting Creditors Control R120 — too large a debit shrank the credit balance too far

questions.question: K. Naidu's R410 invoice captured in the CJ but never posted to her page is fixed by:
options: Adding R410 to the list of creditors — it moves to R6 300

questions.question: Corrections on the creditors side must be re-derived rather than copied from the debtors side because:
options: Creditors balances sit on the credit side, so directions flip — questions are built to punish copiers
The creditors journals use different currencies
Creditors are reconciled annually, not monthly

questions.question: Differences between a supplier's statement and their page in our books arise from:
options: Timing — a payment in transit, an invoice not yet received — and genuine errors on either side

subtopics.title: The Method, Compressed — and Why It Matters

questions.question: If the two correction statements end on different figures:
options: A finding was misclassified or an arithmetic slip made — re-examine before moving on

questions.question: A difference divisible by nine suggests:
options: An amount on the wrong side
Transposed digits somewhere in the copying

questions.question: The figure that flows to the trial balance is:
options: The corrected, agreed balance both statements end on
The larger of the two originals

questions.question: Reconciliation matters as internal control because:
options: It prevents errors from ever happening
It catches inevitable errors within the month, while documents are fresh — mistakes get a one-month lifespan

questions.question: The two witnesses in the case are:
options: The control account's summary line and the added-up personal pages
The trial balance and the budget

questions.question: The R510 difference proves:
options: That the control account is wrong
That at least one error exists — but not where it lives

questions.question: The case must end with:
options: One witness surrendering to the other
Both stories corrected independently until they tell the same truth
The difference written off as sundry expense

subtopics.title: Four Potholes, Each on Its Own Road

questions.question: The column added up R300 short is a pothole in:
options: The totals road — the line goes up R300 to R10 160
The daily road — the pages go up R300

questions.question: The write-off that reached the page but never the totals leaves:
options: The pages expecting money the line has buried
The line still expecting money the pages have buried — line down R260

questions.question: Daniels' page reading R540 for a R450 invoice is patched by:
options: Pages down R90 — only her page exaggerates; the journal line was right

questions.question: After patching, both witnesses read:
options: R9 900 — a truth neither original answer contained

questions.question: The case must close on one number because:
options: Two numbers take up too much space
The shop acts on it tomorrow — trial balance, customer statements, credit decisions
Control accounts may only hold one entry

questions.question: The quiet lesson underneath the case is that:
options: Errors never happen in good businesses
Every error was caught within the month by routine — undiscovered mistakes are the real enemy

questions.question: The supplier's statement is valuable as a third witness because:
options: It was built entirely outside our shop, independent of both our records
It arrives faster than our own books

questions.question: 'Case closed is month closed' means:
options: The shop shuts at month end
The books are locked and never corrected again
Reconciliation is optional once the trial balance levels
The month is only finished once every rand of difference has been explained and one agreed figure carried forward
